additional_projects.title: AirVent — Smart Ventilation System
additional_projects.short_desc: Real-time gas and temperature monitoring with threshold-triggered ventilation and mobile alerts.
additional_projects.summary: AirVent is a smart ventilation system that monitors gas concentration and room temperature in real time. When the gas concentration exceeds a configurable threshold, the ESP32 activates a ventilation fan through a relay and sends a notification to the mobile app. The app displays live gas concentration, lets users adjust the threshold, and provides a concentration-over-time graph.

Flutter App Shell: Hosts the bundled HTML, CSS, and JavaScript dashboard in an Android WebView
Dashboard and Device API: Stores the entered ESP32 IP in browser local storage and offers a local demo mode
Polls the ESP32 HTTP API every second at /api/status
Controls operating mode, fan state, and gas threshold through /api/mode, /api/fan, and /api/threshold
Visualization: Renders live gas readings, threshold status, fan state and runtime, averages, peaks, and a time-series chart

additional_projects.title: CLK-D
additional_projects.short_desc: Arduino Nano clock with a transistor-driven LED matrix, RTC module, buzzer, and ESP-01 for setting the date and time.
additional_projects.summary: CLK-D is an Arduino Nano-based clock that displays the time using an LED matrix. A combination of transistors drives the matrix LEDs. The system includes an RTC module for timekeeping, a buzzer, and an ESP-01 connected to the Arduino Nano to set the date and time.

Hardware: LED matrix driven through a combination of transistors
ESP-01 connected to the Arduino Nano to set the date and time

additional_projects.title: NEXCAM
additional_projects.short_desc: ESP32-CAM wearable device with motion-sensing modes and a companion image-capture app.
additional_projects.summary: NEXCAM is an ESP32-CAM based wearable/handheld device combining motion sensing and camera functionality. It has two modes switched by physical buttons — emoji mode (MPU9250 IMU reads orientation and displays animated emoji faces on OLED based on tilt/motion) and camera mode (boots ESP32-CAM, connects to WiFi, and shows real-time status on OLED). A companion NEXCAM app captures images and stores them locally. Hardware stack: ESP32-CAM, MPU9250 IMU, SSD1306 OLED, two push buttons, and PCF8574 I²C GPIO expander. All I²C devices share a single bus on GPIO 13/14.

Flutter Camera App: Uses the Android CameraX-backed Flutter camera plugin for camera access and still capture
ESP32 Device Connection: Configures Wi-Fi through the /api/wifi HTTP endpoint and reads device status from /api/status
Controls the MJPEG stream through /api/stream?enabled=... and parses incoming JPEG frames

major_projects.title: NAKHWA
major_projects.short_desc: NAKHWA is a smart boat safety and monitoring system designed using IoT, GPS, and LTE technologies. The system uses a custom ESP32 board integrated with the EC200U GSM/GPS module for real-time boat tracking and cloud connectivity.
major_projects.summary: NAKHWA is an advanced smart boat safety and monitoring system designed to enhance maritime safety using IoT, GPS, and LTE communication technologies. The system is built around a custom ESP32-based board integrated with the EC200U GSM/GPS module, enabling real-time location tracking and cloud connectivity. It incorporates multiple sensors including the MPU6050 to measure the boat's pitch and roll for capsizing detection, a flame sensor, temperature sensor, and gas sensor to monitor onboard safety conditions. To reduce false fire alerts caused by environmental factors such as sunlight affecting the flame sensor, the system intelligently cross-verifies data using temperature and gas sensor readings before triggering a fire alert. An SOS emergency button is also integrated, allowing crew members to instantly send emergency notifications to the control center during critical situations. GPS coordinates and sensor data are transmitted over LTE and stored in a Supabase cloud database for real-time monitoring and analytics. A dedicated live dashboard interface displays vessel status, alerts, activity monitoring, and boat locations on a map, enabling authorities or operators to continuously monitor fleet safety and respond quickly during emergencies.

Sensing Layer: Continuously captures: latitude/longitude, roll angle (θ), acceleration (m/s²), angular velocity (°/s)
Temperature (°C), vessel speed (km/h or knots), flame/smoke status
Edge Processing Layer: Embedded Firmware — Real-time sensor interfacing, safety constraint evaluation, alert classification, and communication control
VSCode — Firmware development, compilation, and deployment onto the ESP32
Multi-parameter sensor fusion with configurable safety thresholds (roll threshold, max speed) pushed remotely from the central dashboard
Communication & Control Layer: GSM/GPRS — Transmits sensor data and alerts to the central IoT dashboard; SMS for SOS events
Apache Kafka Streaming Framework — Scalable, low-latency event streaming pipeline for centralized multi-vessel monitoring

Sensor Node: GNSS–GSM Module (EC200U) — Real-time geographic positioning, ground speed estimation, heading, and wireless data transmission
IMU (MPU6050) — Roll and pitch angle computation for vessel stability and motion analysis
Temperature Sensor — Onboard thermal condition monitoring for fire-risk assessment
Smoke Sensor + IR Sensor — Combined combustion detection (smoke + infrared radiation)
SOS Push Button — Manual emergency signaling
Custom ESP32 PCB — All peripherals integrated onto a single board (KiCad designed)

major_projects.title: NEXUS Architecture — Quadranode Rover
major_projects.short_desc: A rugged, fault-tolerant solar-powered rover with a distributed 4-node ESP32 architecture, STM32 RTOS failover, and Raspberry Pi 4B as master server with remote access via Tailscale VPN.
major_projects.summary: The Quadranode Rover is a distributed IoT system designed for rugged outdoor operation. Four ESP32 microcontrollers each own a dedicated function — sensing, actuation, GPS/LTE, and camera. An STM32 Nucleo board running RTOS acts as a hardware failover layer, capable of taking over any failed ESP32 node. A Raspberry Pi 4B serves as the central server, aggregating data from all nodes over MQTT (Mosquitto broker), and exposing remote access through Tailscale VPN. GitHub SSH enables over-the-air firmware updates. The rover is solar powered with dual current/voltage monitoring — one pair tracking solar input, the other tracking real-time power consumption — and an internal thermal management system with auto-cutoff for thermal protection.

Master Node (RPi 4B): Mosquitto MQTT broker for all inter-node communication
Tailscale VPN for secure remote access from anywhere
GitHub SSH for OTA firmware updates to all nodes
Central dashboard aggregating all node telemetry data
Sensor Node Firmware: Reads BH1750, MPU6050, 4× ultrasonic, 2× INA current/voltage pairs, DS18B20
Triggers cooling fan or automatic power cutoff on thermal spike
Actuation Node Firmware: Controls relays, motor drivers, and servos for rover movement and articulation
GPS/LTE Node Firmware: EC200u module for real-time GPS position and LTE uplink
Streams location to RPi for live map tracking
Camera Node Firmware: Pan-tilt servo for 270° field of view coverage
RTOS Failover (STM32): STM32 Nucleo + RTOS monitors all ESP32 nodes
Takes over any crashed node via RTOS task scheduling
LoRa fallback communication when LTE is unavailable

Raspberry Pi 4B: Master server — runs Mosquitto broker, Tailscale VPN, and GitHub SSH agent
4\u00d7 ESP32 Nodes: One per function: Sensor, Actuation, GPS/LTE, Camera
Each independently connected to RPi via MQTT over Wi-Fi/LTE
STM32 Nucleo + RTOS: Watchdog failover board — monitors all ESP32 nodes
Takes over a failed node's function via RTOS task scheduling
Power System: Solar input with dual INA current/voltage pairs — one for solar output, one for consumption monitoring
Thermal Management: Auto cooling fan on threshold breach; automatic power cutoff if temperature continues to rise
EC200u (GPS/LTE) + LoRa: Quectel EC200u for simultaneous GPS fix and 4G LTE uplink
LoRa module as long-range fallback when LTE is unavailable, managed by STM32 RTOS node

major_projects.title: Smart Digital Circuit Breaker
major_projects.short_desc: Developed an IoT-based smart digital circuit breaker using ESP32 and FreeRTOS for real-time electrical monitoring and automated protection. Integrates multiple sensors, SSR relay control, cloud connectivity via Supabase, and a React live web dashboard for remote monitoring and control.
major_projects.summary: Designed and developed an advanced IoT-enabled digital circuit breaker capable of monitoring current, voltage, temperature, and gas levels in real time using an ESP32 microcontroller running FreeRTOS with 6 concurrent tasks. The system features automated circuit protection through 4-channel SSR relay control, offline hardware trip logic, gas leak emergency shutdown, and hysteresis-based relay switching for enhanced safety and stability. A scalable backend was built using Node.js and Supabase, enabling per-board configurable thresholds, AI-based risk scoring, and bidirectional cloud-to-device communication. A React-based industrial dark-theme dashboard was developed to visualize live sensor data, display real-time power charts, configure thresholds, and manually control relays remotely. A 16×2 LCD was integrated to provide live system status and safety alerts directly on the device.

ESP32 Firmware (FreeRTOS): Dual-core ESP32 architecture running 6 concurrent real-time tasks for sensing, safety, cloud communication, and display handling
Mutex-protected shared state synchronization using semaphores to ensure safe multi-core data access without race conditions
Hierarchical safety logic with hardware-level overcurrent and gas protection operating independently of cloud connectivity
Non-blocking DS18B20 temperature acquisition to avoid delays in critical task execution
Resilient cloud communication with automatic WiFi recovery, HTTPS JSON data transfer, AI risk scoring, and local fallback operation
Dashboard (React + Node.js): Futuristic industrial-themed React dashboard for real-time monitoring and control of the digital circuit protection system
Live monitoring of voltage, current, power consumption, temperature, gas levels, AI risk assessment, and cooling fan status
Interactive relay controls with real-time board status indicators and power flow visualization
Historical analytics featuring live power consumption graphs, event logs, and timestamp-based monitoring
Configurable threshold management for power, gas, and temperature limits with cloud-connected synchronization

Sensing Frontend: SCT-013-030 non-invasive CT sensor for current measurement
MQ gas sensor for leak detection
Processing & Display: 16×2 LCD for local power readout and safety alerts
4-channel SSR relay for automated circuit protection

major_projects.title: SafeTrack — Child Safety Tracking System
major_projects.short_desc: Real-time multi-device GPS tracking with geofencing, SOS alerting, and child safety mode. Built with ESP32 + Node.js backend + React dashboard + Supabase.
major_projects.summary: SafeTrack provides a real-time child safety and tracking solution using ESP32 and GPS technology to continuously stream live location data to a cloud dashboard via WiFi and WebSocket communication. It features SOS emergency alerting, where pressing a physical button triggers dashboard notifications, phone calls, and SMS alerts with a Google Maps location link using the SIM800L module. The platform supports geofencing — administrators can create safe zones on a map and receive instant alerts if a child exits the designated area. The system supports multiple devices simultaneously, with independent tracking, SOS monitoring, offline detection, and unique map markers for each device.

ESP32 Firmware: HTTPS POST handler with SSL/TLS secure client communication
Backend (Node.js + Render): Geofence engine using Turf.js for polygon containment checks
Frontend (React + Leaflet): Real-time WebSocket communication for live updates
Multiple map layer support (OSM / Bhuvan / Satellite)
Database (Supabase): Geofence zone polygon storage and breach detection logs

Hardware: ESP32-DevKit — Main MCU. Runs firmware, manages WiFi, reads GPS via UART2, controls button + buzzer via GPIO
NEO-7M GPS — Satellite positioning module. Outputs NMEA sentences at 9600 baud. Provides lat/lng, altitude, speed, fix quality
SIM800L GSM — 2G GSM/GPRS module. Makes voice calls and sends SMS to emergency numbers. Powered at 4V/2A
Push Button — SOS trigger. Wired between GPIO4 and GND with INPUT_PULLUP. Toggle press activates/deactivates SOS
Buzzer — Audio feedback on GPIO2. Plays Morse SOS pattern on alert, beeps on WiFi connect and GPS fix acquired
Power System: 3.7V 3000mAh Li-ion battery as primary power source
MT3608 step-up converter boosts battery voltage to stable 5V
6V 100mA solar panel integrated for portable solar charging
TP4056 charging module for safe Li-ion battery charging and power management

major_projects.title: BlindNav
major_projects.short_desc: IoT navigation assistant for the visually impaired using ESP32, GPS, and a real-time web dashboard
major_projects.summary: BlindNav is a two-phase assistive navigation system built for visually impaired users. Phase 1 combines an ESP32 microcontroller with a NEO-6M GPS module and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to provide real-time location tracking and obstacle detection, with intelligent buzzer patterns for audio feedback. A Node.js backend streams live device data via WebSocket to an interactive Leaflet.js dashboard featuring voice commands, turn-by-turn walking navigation, nearest POI search (hospitals, petrol pumps, pharmacies, etc.), off-route detection, and full text-to-speech guidance — all using free APIs with no API key required. Phase 2 will integrate an ESP32-CAM for object recognition, a MAX98357A amplifier for louder audio output, and a magnetometer for compass-based directional guidance.

sw_arch.deployment: Both services hosted on Render (free tier)

mcu: ESP32 DevKit acts as the central brain — handles WiFi, GPS parsing, obstacle detection, buzzer control, and WebSocket communication all in one chip.
gps: NEO-6M GPS module connected via UART2 (RX=GPIO16, TX=GPIO17) at 9600 baud. Sentences are parsed using TinyGPS++ to extract latitude, longitude, speed, course, satellite count, and HDOP accuracy.
obstacle: HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor on TRIG=GPIO5 and ECHO=GPIO18. Polled every 200ms using a non-blocking millis() timer. Triggers a warning at under 80cm and a danger alert at under 30cm.
audio: Passive buzzer on GPIO26 driven by a fully non-blocking pattern engine. Has 6 distinct patterns — startup chime, GPS searching (double beep), GPS fixed (3 rising beeps), obstacle warning (medium pulse), obstacle danger (rapid pulse), and wrong route (2 descending beeps).
connectivity: ESP32 connects to user WiFi and maintains a persistent WSS WebSocket connection to the Render backend. If WebSocket drops, it automatically falls back to HTTP POST for GPS and obstacle data, and retries WebSocket reconnection every 5 seconds.
phase2_planned: Phase 2 will add an ESP32-CAM for real-time object and sign recognition, a MAX98357A I2S amplifier for loud speaker-grade audio guidance without earphones, and a magnetometer for compass-based turn directions.

protocols: WebSocket (WSS) — live ESP32 to backend to dashboard streaming
HTTP REST — fallback GPS/obstacle POST, place search, routing
UART — ESP32 to NEO-6M GPS at 9600 baud
NMEA 0183 — GPS sentence format parsed by TinyGPS++
OSRM API — open-source walking route calculation
Overpass API — nearby POI queries from OSM data
Web Speech API — browser-side voice recognition and TTS

major_projects.title: CLK-X
major_projects.short_desc: ESP32-S3 smartwatch prototype and Flutter companion with I2C sensors, BLE telemetry and HID controls, phone-assisted features, and OTA updates.
major_projects.summary: CLK-X is a companion-app-driven smartwatch prototype built around an ESP32-S3 Mini and a Flutter phone app. The watch reads MPU6050 motion, BMP280 ambient temperature and pressure, and MAX30102-compatible optical pulse data over a shared I2C bus; it also drives a 128x64 SSD1306 OLED, four physical buttons, a WS2812 status LED, and an optional vibration motor driver. A custom BLE GATT link carries newline-delimited JSON commands and telemetry between the watch and app, while BLE HID lets the watch act as a mouse or keyboard-style presentation controller for a computer. The app handles watch discovery and its first-use PIN check, clock and configuration sync, sensor dashboards and charts, CSV export, trip tracking and maps, and phone-backed camera, media, call, notification, route, and weather features. Watch modes include normal and clock-only operation, motion-controlled HID, the NEXCAM camera remote, and NEXGES rule-based expression feedback. The Arduino firmware runs recurring work in a cooperative loop, targeting 25 Hz motion reads (50 Hz in mouse mode), 5 Hz connected telemetry, and roughly 25 FPS OLED updates; these are scheduling targets, not accuracy or latency guarantees. OTA transfers use a separate raw BLE characteristic and check image size and CRC-32 before applying an update. This remains a prototype: heart rate is an unvalidated beat-detection estimate, SpO2 is not measured, battery percentage is a 100% fallback because no ADC pin is configured, and the app PIN is not BLE encryption or authenticated pairing. Phone GPS and other phone services depend on the handset and its permissions; deep-sleep options shown by the app are not implemented by the current firmware.

ESP32-S3 firmware runtime: C++ firmware built with the Arduino framework and PlatformIO; setup() initializes GPIO, I2C devices, NVS preferences, display, sensors, BLE, and the CLK-X advertising identity.

A cooperative loop() services button events, queued BLE commands, sensors, display, LED and haptic feedback, HID actions, telemetry, screen timeout, and OTA work. It yields with a short delay rather than creating application-owned FreeRTOS tasks.
BLE callbacks hand received commands and OTA chunks to the main loop using FreeRTOS queues and mutexes; NimBLE/ESP-IDF internal scheduling is provided by the platform.

Configured CPU frequency is 80 MHz. Nominal work periods are 40 ms for motion (25 Hz), 20 ms in mouse mode (50 Hz), 200 ms for environment sampling/telemetry (5 Hz), and about 40 ms for OLED rendering (25 FPS; mouse mode targets 20 FPS).
Firmware device and state services: Sensor, button, OLED, WS2812, and optional vibration-driver logic are coordinated by the main loop; sensor presence is probed at startup so an absent module need not prevent other watch functions from starting.
Preferences (ESP32 NVS) persist paired-state, selected mode/configuration, and optional crowd-beacon settings.
Clock-only mode suppresses motion, BMP, and PPG work while BLE and the main loop continue. Display timeout turns off the OLED; it does not put the MCU into deep sleep.
BLE transport and update path: NimBLE-Arduino exposes a custom GATT service; the phone discovers the service and characteristics, subscribes to telemetry, then sends time, configuration, and control commands.
BLE callbacks reassemble newline-delimited UTF-8 JSON command data and enqueue it for loop() processing; notifications carry watch status and sensor telemetry.
A separate OTA characteristic accepts bounded raw image chunks. Firmware checks expected image size, written length, and CRC-32 before finalizing and restarting.
The displayed four-digit PIN is an application-level check, not BLE encryption or authenticated bonding; the report notes that command pairing is not required by default.
Flutter companion application: Dart/Flutter app uses Provider for state, flutter_blue_plus for BLE transport, and a BleLink / WatchController separation between packet handling, watch state, and screens.
Watch, Sensors, Map, Buttons, Modes, and Media screens provide device control, charts, sensor toggles, local configuration, trip history, and CSV export.
Phone-side integrations provide GPS trip tracking and maps, plus camera, media, call, notification, and optional route/weather information; these features depend on phone OS services and permissions.
SharedPreferences stores app configuration and trip data separately from the firmware's NVS state; recent chart data and a rolling sensor log are maintained on the phone.
Mode and sensor behavior: Normal and clock-only watch modes; mouse mode maps wrist tilt and button actions to BLE HID; NEXCAM controls the phone camera; NEXGES displays a threshold-based expression estimate.
The PPG path detects beats and averages a small set of heart-rate estimates; it does not measure SpO2 or provide validated physiological readings.
The app exposes deeper sleep and wake configuration that current firmware does not implement; sensor toggles and display timeout are the supported power-related behaviors.

Controller and target: Generic ESP32-S3 Mini target using the PlatformIO esp32-s3-devkitc-1 profile and Arduino framework; configured CPU frequency is 80 MHz. Confirm the exact board and flash variant before flashing.
The ESP32-S3 coordinates local sensor/display I2C, GPIO inputs/outputs, BLE GATT communication with the phone, and BLE HID interaction with a host computer.
Shared I2C bus (SDA GPIO 8, SCL GPIO 9,: MPU6050 accelerometer/gyroscope: probes 0x68/0x69; configured for +/-8 g and +/-500 degrees/s with an approximately 21 Hz low-pass setting. Read at 25 Hz normally and 50 Hz in mouse mode.
BMP280 environmental sensor: probes 0x76/0x77; supplies ambient temperature and pressure, with altitude derived from a fixed 1013.25 hPa sea-level pressure reference.
MAX30102-compatible optical PPG sensor: initialized through the MAX3010x library and used for demonstration beat/heart-rate estimation only; SpO2 is not implemented.
SSD1306 monochrome OLED: 128x64 display at I2C address 0x3C for the clock, sensor/status pages, pairing/update screens, and interaction feedback.
Physical inputs and outputs: Four active-low buttons on GPIO 4-7 use INPUT_PULLUP and a 30 ms debounce; long presses and button combinations select pages and modes.
WS2812 status/event LED data uses GPIO 10.
Optional vibration motor control is a logic signal on GPIO 11 and requires an external transistor or MOSFET driver; GPIO 11 is not intended to drive the motor directly.
Wireless and power boundaries: Bluetooth Low Energy connects the watch to the Flutter phone app and exposes HID mouse/keyboard behavior to a computer; the documented watch path relies on the phone for GPS, internet, camera, media, and notifications.
Battery ADC is unconfigured (pin -1), so the current firmware cannot measure battery voltage or charging state and reports fallback values.

Firmware and App: ESP32-S3 Mini firmware built with the Arduino framework using the PlatformIO esp32s3devkitc1 profile; verify the exact board and flash variant before flashing.
Flutter phone companion connected to the watch over BLE; phone-side GPS, camera, media, and notification features depend on their corresponding OS services and permissions.
Hardware and Interfaces: SSD1306 128x64 OLED, MPU6050, BMP280, and MAX30102-compatible PPG sensor on the shared I2C bus: SDA GPIO8, SCL GPIO9, 400 kHz.
Four active-low buttons on GPIO4-GPIO7; WS2812 status/event LED on GPIO10; optional vibration motor control on GPIO11 requires an external transistor or MOSFET driver.
Core Behaviors: BLE scan/connect, first-use four-digit PIN, paired-state persistence, clock/time synchronization, connection and firmware status, and OTA updates checked by size and CRC-32.
Phone app provides Watch, Sensors, Map, Buttons, Modes, and Media tabs, with charts, CSV export, sensor toggles, local configuration, and optional route/weather integration.
Implementation Limits: Battery ADC is not configured; the reported 100% is a fallback and charging status is not measured.
SpO2 is not measured, and the heart-rate path is basic beat detection rather than a validated medical measurement.
Deep sleep, hibernate, shake/timer wake, night schedule, and generic per-button action settings are not implemented by the current firmware.

minor_projects.name: Audio Visualizer
minor_projects.desc: ESP32-based Audio Monitoring and Visualization System using three INMP MEMS microphones capturing surrounding sound from multiple directions. Processes real-time audio data on the ESP32 and visualizes live waveforms, FFT spectrum analysis, microphone intensity levels, and sound direction on an OLED display as well as a custom web dashboard.

minor_projects.name: Mini Oscilloscope
minor_projects.desc: Mini Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) using Arduino Nano capable of capturing and visualizing electrical waveforms on a 0.96-inch OLED. Features real-time signal sampling, waveform processing, trigger handling, and input protection (resistor dividers, Zener clamping). Four push buttons and 10k potentiometer for menu navigation and scaling. Portable power management using 3.7V Li-ion battery, TP4056 charging module, and MT3608 step-up converter.

minor_projects.name: Environment Monitoring System
minor_projects.desc: IoT-based Environmental Monitoring System using ESP32 integrating MQ Gas Sensor, PM2.5 Sensor, BMP280, DHT22, BH1750 Light Sensor, and voltage/current sensing modules connected to a 12V solar panel. ESP32 hosts a live monitoring dashboard as a local web server. BH1750 measures solar intensity while V/I sensors monitor panel output — comparing both to evaluate solar efficiency. Integrated with Thynk Cloud for remote graphical monitoring.

minor_projects.name: Smart Study Desktop Lamp
minor_projects.desc: Smart Desktop Lamp using ESP32 integrating smart lighting, environmental monitoring, and wireless audio. 20×4 LCD shows real-time temperature, humidity, pressure, time, and date via Wi-Fi. Functions as a Bluetooth speaker with PAM amplifier and 2 speakers. Audio-reactive WS2812B RGB LED strip syncs animations and colors with music frequency and intensity. LDR-based automatic night lamp auto-activates below ambient light threshold. Powered by 3.7V Li-ion battery with TP4056 + MT3608.

minor_projects.name: Smart Weather Station
minor_projects.desc: DHT11 + BMP280 sensors pushing real-time humidity, temperature, and pressure to a webpage hosted on ESP32 acting as a local server. Dual charging support from a solar panel and a 12V adaptor keeps the station always powered.

minor_projects.name: RC BOT
minor_projects.desc: Long-range 10-channel RF Transmitter and Receiver System using nRF24L01 antenna modules for wireless communication and control. Built a multifunctional RC Rover capable of operating over an approximate range of 1 kilometre with stable real-time control.

minor_projects.name: Wi-Fi Controlled Car
minor_projects.desc: ESP32-based Wi-Fi controlled robotic car where the ESP32 acts as a local server hosting a wireless dashboard for real-time vehicle control. Features a dual steering mechanism combining Ackermann steering for smooth directional movement and rover-style differential steering for sharp turns. Powered by a 12V 8000mAh rechargeable battery.

minor_projects.name: Smart RGB Lamp
minor_projects.desc: NodeMCU-based Smart RGB Lamp using WS2812 addressable LEDs integrated with the WLED platform for wireless lighting control and customization. Controls brightness, colors, patterns, animations, and lighting effects through the WLED dashboard over Wi-Fi.
